answer: Identity registration runs through a trellis: each new agent bonds stake to three randomly drawn existing peers who vouch under their own collateral, so no operator can vouch for itself. A prism step then refracts every claim into separate attestations that must agree. Cloning identities means planting an orchard of independent bonds and persuading unrelated peers to risk collateral on each one, so faking N agents costs N times the stake plus N peer-vouch overhead—strictly more than one honest registration pays.
